hits.text:
Meta Muse will probably create 1000+ millionaires

This is the most slept on arbitrage I’ve seen in years and it’s not even close.

Here’s how i’d build a 1 person business powered by AI/Muse with with $0 and 0 social following https://t.co/99uf6B7Xvn

hits.draft_en:
Greg Isenberg says Meta Muse will create 1000+ millionaires and called it the most slept-on arbitrage in years. 1.08M views and 24k bookmarks.

The bookmarks are the real signal: people save a step-by-step plan for a 1 person business with $0 and no following.

Ignore the millionaire number. Keep the useful part: pick one boring task a local business pays for, build it with a new model this week, and show one real customer using it.

What would you build first with $0?
hits.video_tip: 12s: a blank notebook titled '$0, 0 followers', three steps writing themselves, then a single customer message popping up, caption one real customer beats a million views.

I asked M3.1 Flash (left) and Opus 5.5 (right) to build me a landing page for a hardware device launch.

hits.quote_note: @MiniMax_AI: MiniMax M3.1 Flash: Space Performance + Bunny Speed  🚀🐰 Yes, Space Bunny  - which has topped global  (1,119,292)
hits.draft_en:
Hassan ran the same landing page prompt through MiniMax M3.1 Flash and Claude Opus 5.5. 120k views.

His numbers: $0.014 vs $1.22, about 88x cheaper and 4x faster on his test.

That is one test, not a benchmark. But it is the right habit: before you pick a model for a product, run your own prompt through two of them and compare cost per output.

What is the cheapest model that is good enough for your job?
hits.video_tip: 10s: split screen of two landing pages building side by side, cost counters ticking $0.014 vs $1.22, caption run your own test.

Yohei Nakajima: someone offered him tens of thousands of de-identified patient records, biomarkers and medical history. Who are the buyers? 28k views.

virals.angle: Test the cheap model on your own prompt
virals.draft_en:
Hassan ran one landing page prompt through MiniMax M3.1 Flash and Claude Opus 5.5. On his test it cost $0.014 vs $1.22 and ran 4x faster.

MiniMax's launch post hit 1.1M views. OpenAI's Codex showcase hit 1.5M. Everyone is selling the model.

You don't need a leaderboard. Take the one prompt your product runs most, send it to two models, and write down cost, time and whether you would ship the output. Thirty minutes, and you know your real number.
virals.inspired_by: @nutlope M3.1 Flash vs Opus 5.5 (121k) + @MiniMax_AI launch (1.12M) + @OpenAIDevs Codex showcase (1.54M)
virals.video_tip: 12s: one prompt card splitting into two model lanes, cost and time counters, a check mark on the one you'd ship, caption test your own prompt.

virals.angle: AI coding just hit the normal office
virals.draft_en:
Pieter's friend works a regular software job at a traditional company in a small Austrian town. This week he said: everything takes 5 seconds now, and his employer plans to cancel a $10K a year CMS and build their own dashboard.

The same day Theo wrote that his vibe coded pieces collapsed overnight and engineers are still very much necessary.

Both are true. AI makes the first 80% fast. Someone still has to own the last 20%. If you're that person at a normal company, you're about to be very valuable.
virals.inspired_by: @levelsio Austria friend AI-pilled (54k) + @theo 'engineers are still very, very much necessary' (145k) + @marclou '80/20 AGI' (92k)
virals.video_tip: 10s: a progress bar racing to 80% then crawling, a person stepping in to finish it, caption the last 20% is the job.

virals.angle: Turn a small annoyance into a same-day build
virals.draft_en:
Pieter wanted coffee jazz on his Alexa without paying for Spotify. He posted the complaint (72k views), then 'OK why not' with an agent working on it (66k), then 'it works' an hour later (16k).

Three posts, one small problem, one morning.

Pick one annoying thing in your home or workflow today. Post the problem, post the first attempt, post the result. People follow the story, not the launch.
virals.inspired_by: @levelsio HomePod question (72k) + 'OK why not' (66.5k) + Alexa skill works (16k)
virals.video_tip: 12s: three phone screens in sequence, problem, attempt, fixed, each with a timestamp an hour apart, caption build it before lunch.

virals.angle: The cheap-and-boring one-person business, minus the hype
virals.draft_en:

drafts.angle: Test the cheap model on your own prompt
drafts.draft_en:
Hassan ran one landing page prompt through MiniMax M3.1 Flash and Claude Opus 5.5. On his test it cost $0.014 vs $1.22 and ran 4x faster.

MiniMax's launch post hit 1.1M views. OpenAI's Codex showcase hit 1.5M. Everyone is selling the model.

You don't need a leaderboard. Take the one prompt your product runs most, send it to two models, and write down cost, time and whether you would ship the output. Thirty minutes, and you know your real number.

Both are true. AI makes the first 80% fast. Someone still has to own the last 20%. If you're that person at a normal company, you're about to be very valuable.

drafts.angle: Turn a small annoyance into a same-day build
drafts.draft_en:
Pieter wanted coffee jazz on his Alexa without paying for Spotify. He posted the complaint (72k views), then 'OK why not' with an agent working on it (66k), then 'it works' an hour later (16k).

Three posts, one small problem, one morning.

Pick one annoying thing in your home or workflow today. Post the problem, post the first attempt, post the result. People follow the story, not the launch.
